sentences.text: The brief facts of the present case are that the petitioners, as well as, the respondent no.2 had entered into a joint venture and in the course of business of that joint venture certain funds were misappropriated by the petitioners.
The respondent no. 2 made a complaint which led to the registration of aforesaid FIR.
7. It is an admitted case of the parties that a Civil Suit i.e., CS (COMM) 616/2017 had been filed by the respondent no.2 against the petitioners in this court.

8. During the pendency of the said suit, the parties were referred to the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre, where the parties have arrived at a settlement, terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of the Settlement Agreement dated 03.09.2021.

In terms of the aforesaid settlement, it was agreed that the petitioners shall pay an amount of Rs.61,47,600/- (Rupees Sixty One Lakh Forty Seven Thousand Six Hundred Only) to the firm of the respondent no.2 namely i.e.,
M/s. Jegson Publicity at New Delhi towards full and final settlement of all claims of the firm of the respondent no.2.
9.
The aforesaid amount of Rs. 61,47,600/- has been paid by the petitioners to the said firm of the respondent no.2, the receipt of which respondent no.2 acknowledges.
10. Further, pursuant to the settlement, the cross-suits filed by the petitioners, as well as, by the respondent no.2 through his firm, have been This is a digitally signed order.

11. On a query made by this court, the respondent no.2 states that he has entered into a compromise out of his own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
He further states that he has no objection in case the present FIR is quashed.

12. It is trite that the criminal proceedings which essentially have a civil flavour as distinguished from the proceedings involving serious criminal offences or heinous crimes can be quashed in exercise of the jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC.
13.
At this juncture, it may be apt to advert to the legal position as regards the quashing of FIR premised on a settlement or where the conviction of the accused is a distant possibility.

In Madhavrao Jiwajirao Scindia and Ors. Vs. Sambhajirao Chandrojirao Angre and Ors. (1998) 1 SCC 692, it was held as under:-
"7.The

It is also for the court to take into consideration any special features which appear in a particular case to consider whether it is expedient and in the interest of justice to permit a Srishti Gupta & Anr vs State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175959515/

sentences.text: This is so on the basis that the court cannot be utilised for any oblique purpose and where in the opinion of the court chances of an ultimate conviction is bleak and, therefore, no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution to continue, the court may while taking into consideration the special facts of a case also quash the proceeding even though it may be at a preliminary stage.

"...16.7.
As distinguished from serious offences, there may be criminal cases which have an overwhelming or predominant element of a civil dispute.
They stand on a distinct footing insofar as the exercise of the inherent power to quash is concerned.

16.8. Criminal cases involving offences which arise from commercial, financial,
mercantile, partnership or similar transactions with an essentially civil flavour may in appropriate situations fall for quashing where parties have settled the dispute.

16.9. In such a case, the High Court may quash the criminal proceeding if in view of the compromise between the disputants, the possibility of a conviction is remote and the continuation of a criminal proceeding would cause oppression and prejudice;
and"...

15. Keeping in view, the above legal position and regard being had to the fact that the FIR is an outcome of commercial venture jointly undertaken by the petitioners and respondent no. 2, it is a case with an essentially civil flavour.
Further, in view of the settlement, the chances of conviction of the petitioners, are bleak.
Therefore, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the criminal proceedings.
16. In view of the above, the petition is allowed.
Accordingly, the FIR No.561/2015 under Sections 420/468/471/120B/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Mianwali Nagar is quashed along with all other consequential proceedings emanating there from.

17. Since the machinery of the State has been put into motion which led to the registration of the FIR and now, the charge sheet has also been filed, it is deemed appropriate that some costs be imposed on the petitioners.
Accordingly, the petitioners are directed to deposit an amount of Rs.25,000/- in the Delhi High Court Staff Welfare Fund.
